subject: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@clearwave.com>, Tom Barlow <tbarlow@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps

Elena, Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I attached a first-pass MAP and an accompanying acceptance-test list to make the evaluation deterministic and reduce ambiguity at close. High-level asks:

- Confirm the priority KPIs below and tell us which 1–2 metrics you want to treat as the deal "go/no-go" signals.
- Review the proposed exit gates and the failure-mode checklist (rollback/mitigation).
- Share any procurement constraints or compliance checks that would block cutover.

Proposed success signals (we recommend choosing 1 primary + 1 secondary):
1) 95th percentile inference latency < 250ms for 95% of API calls in peak window (30-min rolling).
2) Average cost per 1k tokens within 20% of the committed target in pilot run.
3) End-to-end accuracy on your sampled dataset: macro F1 >= 0.82 for labeled tasks (synced to your 300-case set).

Exit gates (must pass all to progress to pilot close):
- Reliability: No more than 1 incident causing >10% request failures in a 24h window during week-long validation.
- Security: SOC 2 artifact checklist completed and evidence uploaded to your portal.
- Data handling: KV cache behavior documented and approved for PII patterns in sample logs.

Failure-mode checklist (quick examples):
- Latency regression: Fall back to smaller quantized model, flag affected routes, and run mitigation A/B for 48h.
- Cost spike: Throttle burst traffic, enable aggressive caching for the 12h window while we triage.

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (milestones + owners), acceptance-test-cases.md (detailed test steps). I put a HubSpot link to the MAP in the Drive folder in case you want to edit collaboratively.

Next step: can you confirm the primary KPI by Monday so we can lock the test harness?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), acceptance-test-cases.md (text)

From: Elena Soto <elena@clearwave.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Tom Barlow <tbarlow@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps

On Fri, 05 Sep 2026 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena, Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I attached a first-pass MAP and an accompanying acceptance-test list to make the evaluation deterministic and reduce ambiguity at close.

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. Quick responses from my side:

- Primary KPI: we'll treat E2E accuracy (macro F1) on the labeled 300-case set as the primary go/no-go. Secondary KPI: 95th pctl latency.
- Procurement: net-30 payment terms are standard; procurement@clearwave.com will need to review the SLA before legal signs. Expect a formal checklist by Wed.
- Security: we have a small privacy concern around KV cache dumps. Marcus — can your team confirm that sample logs will be redacted and that caching is configurable at the route level?

One ask: add an explicit rolling-window definition to the MAP for the latency KPI (e.g., 30-min rolling, as you suggested) and a pass/fail threshold for the weekly test run. Also: include a short rollback runbook step for the scenario where accuracy drops below 0.78 (we'd like an automatic pause + notification).

I'll loop procurement on the formal SLA request.

—Elena
Director of Data Products, Clearwave Health

Attachments: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Elena Soto <elena@clearwave.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps

Elena — short answers:

- KV cache: yes. We can apply redaction rules on ingestion and avoid caching fields flagged as PII. We'll provide a sample redacted log and an option to disable KV caching per-route during the pilot.
- Latency rolling window: we'll instrument with 30-min rolling 95th pctl and publish a dashboard with alerts on breach.
- Accuracy rollback: we'll add an automated pause trigger if macro F1 < 0.78 for two consecutive daily runs; on pause, traffic will be routed to your current model endpoint (no-lock fallback) and we will open an incident with remediation steps.

I'll attach a brief mitigation runbook and ping infra to prepare the dashboard templates. Naomi — can we add a short milestone: "validation run complete and dashboard verified" on Sep 16? That gives us a week to finalize tests after you confirm the KPI.

Marcus
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.md (text stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@clearwave.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, procurement@clearwave.com
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps

Perfect — thanks Marcus and Elena. I've updated the MAP_v1.xlsx with the clarified rolling-window definition and added a small section called "Failure-mode automatic actions" per Marcus's runbook. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPfolder

Proposed timeline (lightweight):
- Sep 10: Clearwave confirms primary KPI (Elena) and procurement sends SLA ask.
- Sep 13–15: Instrumentation & integration window (set up dashboard, ingest 300-case labeled set).
- Sep 16: Validation run complete + dashboard verification (internal sign-off).
- Sep 17–19: Pilot week (production-like traffic slice).
- Sep 20: Close review — pass/fail decision and commercial close steps.

Open items I will own: final MAP workbook update, coordinate procurement ask, and confirm the test harness details with Marcus.

Can procurement loop in legal if there are non-standard terms?

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (updated)

From: procurement@clearwave.com <procurement@clearwave.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Elena Soto <elena@clearwave.com>
Cc: Tom Barlow <tbarlow@clearwave.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outcomes & failure-mode checklist for evaluation — MAP + close steps

Hi Naomi / team — procurement here. We reviewed the SLA_proposal.pdf and have two ask items before we sign:

1) Add a 45-day audit response SLA clause (our compliance team requires evidence within that window).
2) Clarify data retention defaults for logs used during evaluation — we need a max 90-day retention for evaluation logs unless otherwise approved.

If Redwood can accept those two items, we'll route the document to legal and aim for review by Sep 14. Otherwise we'll flag exceptions.

Please let us know and we can draft the redline.

procurement@clearwave.com
Clearwave Health — Procurement
